evidence.quotation: H. All other parts of this instrument come into force on 15 July 2026

explicitRequirements.text: This rule applies where a borrower has failed to make a payment by the time it has fallen due under the terms of a regulated deferred payment credit agreement (‘a missed payment’).
explicitRequirements.note: Condition precedent: rule applies only where a borrower has a missed payment under a regulated deferred payment credit agreement.

explicitRequirements.text: Notify the borrower that the missed payment occurred and about unpaid sums (including non-compliance charges).
explicitRequirements.parentTiming: As soon as possible after a missed payment has occurred (CONC 7.20.1R(2)).

explicitRequirements.text: Provide the borrower with sufficient information to understand the agreement, adverse consequences (actual and likely), and mitigation steps where relevant.
explicitRequirements.parentTiming: As soon as possible after a missed payment has occurred (CONC 7.20.1R(2)).

explicitRequirements.text: The information required under (2) must be provided together.
In this rule references to ‘payment’ refer to the repayment of capital but exclude payment of a charge for non-compliance with a regulated deferred payment credit agreement.
explicitRequirements.note: Definition limb — not a standalone operational obligation.

interpretativeTopics.regulatoryText: As soon as possible after a missed payment has occurred the firm must:
interpretativeTopics.platformStance: Do not invent a day-count SLA. Record the statutory wording and escalate timing standards to compliance/legal expert review.

interpretativeTopics.regulatoryText: …provide the borrower with sufficient information for the borrower to understand…
interpretativeTopics.platformStance: Outcome-based standard. Firm must judge sufficiency per case; expert review on defensible content and channel.

interpretativeTopics.regulatoryText: Any adverse consequences arising … and any that the firm considers are likely to arise…
interpretativeTopics.platformStance: Rule does not enumerate consequences. Escalate which consequences must be disclosed (charges, credit reporting, enforcement, etc.).

interpretativeTopics.regulatoryText: …adverse consequences … that the firm considers are likely to arise…
interpretativeTopics.platformStance: Requires firm judgement and evidence of that judgement. Escalate governance for documenting "likely" consequences.

interpretativeTopics.regulatoryText: (where relevant) any steps the borrower can take to mitigate those adverse consequences.
interpretativeTopics.platformStance: Firm decides when mitigation is relevant. No invented list of steps.

interpretativeTopics.regulatoryText: No transitional material in the instrument references this provision. This is a text search, not a legal conclusion on in-flight agreements or temporary-permission firms.
interpretativeTopics.platformStance: Commencement for the rule is traced to instrument clause H (15 July 2026) unless superseded by transitional material. Text search found no provision-specific transitional reference; expert confirmation still required for in-flight agreements.
